interpretation_note: Receptor with broad non-neural and epithelial associations; increased signal does not establish neural origin.
Integrin alpha-1 participates in adhesion across stromal and other cell types; this association is not a source-cell assignment.
Associated with oligodendrocyte progenitors, but also mesenchymal and other non-neural cells; a PDGFRA signal cannot establish oligodendroglial EV origin.
Neural adhesion association is not neuronal EV proof. Soluble L1CAM in human plasma is a major interpretation caveat; assess EV association rather than assuming L1CAM signal identifies neuronal EVs.
NCAM1 has neural associations and is also expressed by NK cells and other non-neural populations; CD56 signal alone cannot identify neuronal EV origin.
Aminopeptidase with myeloid, stromal and additional tissue associations; do not interpret this as an exclusive myeloid or neural lineage label.
Found in endothelial, platelet and leukocyte contexts; plasma signal cannot distinguish vascular EVs from platelet or leukocyte-associated material.
Mannose-6-phosphate/IGF2 receptor with broad trafficking functions; no source-cell assignment is supported by this marker alone.
Associated with microglia and peripheral myeloid cells; this assay cannot use CD11b alone to distinguish microglial from peripheral myeloid material.
Glycosylated surface antigen with hematopoietic and epithelial associations; expression is not restricted to neural cells.
Leukocyte-associated phosphatase, including microglia; plasma CD45 signal does not separate CNS-resident from peripheral immune sources.
Shared progenitor/epithelial association rather than a neuron or glia identity. The CD133/1 antibody recognizes a particular epitope; signal can depend on epitope accessibility and glycosylation.
Glycolipid-reactive O4 epitope associated with oligodendroglial differentiation, not a single gene product. This interpretive association does not validate cellular origin in precipitated plasma.
GLAST/EAAT1 is associated with astroglial glutamate transport, but expression and epitope availability must be considered; a plasma assay signal alone does not prove astrocyte EV origin.
Shared neuronal and stromal/fibroblast associations; interpretation depends on context and cannot identify a donor-cell lineage from this bead signal.
Expressed in microglial and peripheral immune contexts, including monocytes; CX3CR1 does not distinguish microglial from peripheral myeloid EV sources.
Broad growth-factor receptor with epithelial and neural-progenitor associations; it is not a neural-origin readout.
Broad lymphatic endothelial/stromal and other tissue associations; signal should not be assigned to a neural lineage.
Recognizes ganglioside epitope(s), not a single gene product. Associations include neurons and glial progenitors; these developmental/contextual associations do not identify EV cell of origin.
Widely expressed integrin beta-1 with broad adhesion functions; this marker does not resolve a source cell type.
NG2/CSPG4 has oligodendrocyte progenitor, pericyte and additional mesenchymal/tumor associations; a positive signal cannot establish an oligodendroglial EV origin.
Common EV-associated tetraspanin and optional reference candidate, not a universal EV marker. Expression and detection vary across EV populations; normalization is a separate quantitative decision.

EV-associated/endolysosomal tetraspanin with platelet-associated contexts, not a universal EV marker. Signal can reflect population and activation differences; annotation does not enable normalization.
Common EV-associated tetraspanin with broad cellular expression, not a universal EV marker. It cannot assign neural origin or independently quantify all EVs.
Broadly expressed cell-surface receptor involved in immune regulation and adhesion, including blood-cell contexts; no unique origin inference is supported.
Polysialylated NCAM epitope associated with neural development/plasticity, not a separate single-gene marker. Non-neural expression and glycosylation context limit origin interpretation.
Broad adhesion receptor across immune, stromal and other populations; it does not identify astrocytes or another neural lineage in plasma.
Broad activation/metabolic associations, especially in immune contexts; marker signal is not an exclusive immune or neural-origin measurement.
Integrin alpha-6/laminin receptor with epithelial and progenitor associations; shared expression precludes source-cell assignment.
Adhesion molecule associated with endothelial activation and stromal contexts; a signal does not establish endothelial or neural EV origin.
Integrin alpha-5/fibronectin receptor has broad adhesion and stromal associations; this is an interpretive category, not an origin measurement.
Adhesion/activation-associated molecule in immune, endothelial and other contexts; signal cannot resolve cellular origin.
Scavenger receptor in platelet, peripheral myeloid and microglial contexts; plasma CD36 signal is not a selective microglia readout and may have platelet-associated contributions.
Lysosomal membrane protein with surface exposure in degranulation/trafficking contexts; signal and accessibility do not define a cell lineage.
Endolysosomal/myeloid-associated marker in macrophage and microglial contexts; CD68 cannot distinguish microglia from peripheral myeloid sources in this assay.

Vesicular glutamate transporter with glutamatergic neuronal associations. Vesicular localization and antibody epitope accessibility/topology require validation in intact captured EVs; signal alone does not establish neuronal EV origin.
Assay background diagnostic, not a biological marker or EV lineage measurement. It does not replace the matched no-EV assay blank.
Ganglioside lipid epitope, not a single gene product; neural/developmental and non-neural tumor associations do not establish neuronal or glial EV origin in plasma.
Assay background diagnostic, not a biological marker or EV lineage measurement. It does not replace the matched no-EV assay blank.
